Their positive-volume intersection is exactly hT by the nonnegative-coordinate and coordinate-sum inequalities, with h=0 handled by an empty retained set.

A through-mark cap gives thresholds t,0,-t with one fixed continuous normal after the shear. The accepted weighted centroid-tail inequality applies to E⊂cK on the left and cK at the middle and right. The rest of the middle cap is (1-c^d) times the original K-cap and pays Γ(1-c^d)V.

For a pure-base cap through base 2 the middle and one neighbor remain, giving at least (1+b^d)V. The omitted base 0 can contribute only nonnegative volume. Null additional fibers change neither the caps nor total M.

The frozen scalar inequality has exactly the required domain and its positive part is (1+1/d)h. After multiplying by Γ/2, adding Γ/2 and substituting a≤2b-1, it gives the claimed comparison with ΓM/2. This normalization was also checked on the 2,312 rational radius samples.

The original margin on m_z+r_zX dominates the comparison margin on r_jv+r_z(X-v) by the touching lower-support inequality. Both coordinates use Jacobian r_z^d. The vertex permutation fixes the centered simplex, has determinant of absolute value one, and maps the comparison family to the same common-vertex profile for every normal.

Checked concavity of the radius roof from consecutive midpoint inclusions, so the common-vertex family is actual. The statements match 8f194c2219f76d2a §§1–2 and the independently internalized comparison in 24467ade6f021ae8 §§2–4.

Actual convexity verifies every anchored Minkowski inclusion on the four sampled bases. Apply to direction -u/||u|| at j=2, then multiply by -||u|| to obtain the touching affine minorant of the lower supports.
